text.title: How a Concept Gate Stops Gating
text.summary: Six ways the PR/FAQ degrades into paperwork, each with the observable symptom and the rule that prevents it.

failure.symptom: Every concept that entered the gate proceeded. The document is described internally as "a formality" or "the thing you write before you start".
failure.cause: `kill` was treated as a failure of the review rather than an outcome of it, so authors wrote until the answer came out `proceed`.
failure.prevention: Record `kill` as a successful run with its phase. A gate with no kills in its history has selected for documents that survive it, not for concepts worth building.

failure.symptom: The review produces 7.5/10, then 8, then a decision to proceed "since it's borderline anyway". Nobody can reconstruct what changed.
failure.cause: A number was emitted. Numbers are arguable by whoever wants the answer, and the argument leaves no record.
failure.prevention: Judgement plus written rationale, no numeric field under any name. The validator rejects `score`, `rating`, `confidence` and their synonyms outright.

failure.symptom: The announcement reads like a roadmap item. Reviewers agree it sounds good and nobody can say what would be different for anyone.
failure.cause: Future tense lets a benefit be gestured at without being committed to. "Will streamline collaboration" needs no customer; "now closes the month in one afternoon instead of three days" needs one.
failure.prevention: Past tense, dated availability, forbidden forward-looking verbs, one customer quote. The validator greps for the verb forms.

failure.symptom: A single FAQ of eight friendly questions. Cost is absent, the incumbent is unnamed, and no question is uncomfortable.
failure.cause: The two banks were merged, which removes the antagonist — the customer FAQ sells, and with nothing interrogating it the document is only a sales document.
failure.prevention: Two separate banks, five questions minimum each, at least one the author would rather not answer, and every kill-assumption listed under `must_be_true`.

failure.symptom: An internal platform is validated by enthusiasm in the design review; an OSS release by stars; a nonprofit programme by beneficiary gratitude. All three ship and then fail on something nobody measured.
failure.cause: The success measure was inherited from a commercial template while the concept type was not commercial, so the party who can actually kill it — the funding team, the second maintainer, the funder — was never asked.
failure.prevention: Declare `concept_type`; the success measure must name the antagonist that type implies. Stars are not maintainers and gratitude is not funding.

failure.symptom: The customer field says "developers" or "small businesses". Three phases later the review is still arguing about who this is for, and the argument is called scoping.
failure.cause: An unnameable customer was allowed past phase 1, so every subsequent phase was written against a placeholder that each reader filled differently.
failure.prevention: Stop at phase 1 after two exchanges without a nameable customer. That kill costs one phase; discovering the same thing after a build costs the build.
